On a standard t with n in row r_i, only column permutations fixing n contribute to theta_i(e_t); they give exactly e_(t minus n). For n in an earlier removable row, its corner column has height that row, so no column permutation puts n in row r_i and theta_i(e_t)=0. Deleted standard tableaux run through the full standard basis of S_F^(lambda^(i)); compare field-uniform basis vectors on both sides to identify the kernel exactly. Equivariance follows from the definition of theta_i. Finite constructions use no arbitrary choice; the cited prerequisites are published or earlier ready local items.
